summary: api.py enumerates API surface (OpenAPI/Swagger, GraphQL, SOAP/WSDL, gRPC ServerReflection), parses specs, probes spec-marked-secured endpoints for broken auth and BOLA/IDOR, and lifts embedded credentials out of spec bodies into the credential store. Mostly T1 with one clean T2 (embedded credentials captured). Biggest gap: no follow-through on the captured spec — every unauth-secured endpoint / mutation name is a candidate but no injection/BOLA sweep runs against it beyond the basic id=1 vs id=2 diff.

findings.title_pattern: API endpoints reachable without authentication (broken auth)
findings.tier_evidence: Spec-declared-secured endpoint returned 200 with no credential AND body length > 8 — deterministic broken-auth signal.
findings.promotion_notes: For each unauth-200 endpoint, fetch a larger body sample and mine for user records / PII / secrets — captured data is T2 (proof of read).
findings.tester_next_step: for p in $(jq -r '.paths|keys[]' spec.json); do curl -sSk http://IP:PORT$p | jq . | head -40; done

findings.tier_evidence: id=1 vs id=2 return different-length bodies unauth — deterministic BOLA candidate.
findings.promotion_notes: Sweep id 1..500, hash bodies, count distinct records — record count is data-extraction proof (T2).
findings.tester_next_step: for i in $(seq 1 500); do curl -sSk -o /tmp/u$i http://IP:PORT/api/users/$i; done ; md5sum /tmp/u* | sort -u -k1,1 | wc -l

findings.title_pattern: Credentials embedded in the API spec
findings.tier_evidence: _URL_CRED_RE extracts real user:pw pairs from the spec and pushes Credential objects — extracted material.
findings.promotion_notes: Spray captured user:pw against the API's own login/auth endpoint and the spec's declared servers (often DB URIs) → T3 foothold.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/openapi.json | grep -Eo '://[^:/@ ]+:[^@/ ]{3,}@' ; # then spray against DB / SSH / basic-auth panels

findings.promotion_notes: Already promoted via _enumerate/_spec_findings; add param-fuzzing per operation for injection.
findings.tester_next_step: curl -sSk http://IP:PORT/openapi.json | jq '.paths|keys' ; feed to postman/burp for full surface fuzzing

findings.tier_evidence: Full __schema returned — schema map, not exploitation.
findings.promotion_notes: For every mutation name, POST a benign call unauth and record 200 with a non-error body — successful unauth mutation = T2 write proof.

findings.tier_evidence: Array query returned 2 results (surface signal only).
findings.promotion_notes: Batch 100 login mutations in one HTTP request to bypass per-request rate limiting → T1 credential-brute amplification.
Auto-invoke each operation with default-typed args and check for 200/soap:Fault — unauth reachable ops → T1.
findings.tester_next_step: wsdler <wsdl-url> ; then for op in operations: SoapUI test or curl -X POST -d '<soap:Envelope>...'

findings.tier_evidence: Server responds to gRPC reflection call.
findings.promotion_notes: grpcurl list + describe + call each service unauth; 200/OK on a data-returning RPC = T1 broken-auth.
findings.tester_next_step: grpcurl -plaintext IP:PORT list ; grpcurl -plaintext IP:PORT describe SomeService ; grpcurl -plaintext -d '{}' IP:PORT SomeService.GetAll

findings.promotion_notes: Same surface as OpenAPI spec once loaded; nothing new.
findings.tester_next_step: xdg-open http://IP:PORT/swagger-ui/ ; drive by hand or via Postman import from /openapi.json
